hints: Use $\cos(\angle BAO) = \frac{6}{8} = 0.75$ and solve for angle in radians.
walkthrough:
In the isosceles triangle $\triangle AOB$ (with $OA = OB = 8\text{ cm}$ and $AB = 12\text{ cm}$), drop a perpendicular from apex $O$ to the midpoint of the base $AB$:
$$\cos(\angle BAO) = \frac{\frac{1}{2}(12)}{8} = \frac{6}{8} = 0.75$$

Calculate the angle in radians to 3 significant figures:
$$\angle BAO = \cos^{-1}(0.75) \approx 0.72273 \approx 0.723\text{ radians}$$

hints: Subtract triangle area from sector area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of sector $ABC$ (centred at $A$ with radius $12\text{ cm}$ and angle $\angle BAC = 0.72273\text{ radians}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(12^2)(0.72273) = 72 \times 0.72273 \approx 52.0368\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of triangle $\triangle AOB$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle AOB) = \frac{1}{2}(OA)(AB)\sin(\angle BAO) = \frac{1}{2}(8)(12)\sin(0.72273) \approx 48(0.66144) \approx 31.7490\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to find the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) - \text{Area}(\triangle AOB) = 52.0368 - 31.7490 = 20.2878 \approx 20.3\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

hints: Calculate $OC = AC - AO = 12 - 8 = 4\text{ cm}$ and $OB = 8\text{ cm}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the circular arc length $BC$ of the sector:
$$\text{Arc } BC = r\theta = 12 \times 0.72273 \approx 8.6728\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the straight segment $OC$ along the diameter/line $AOC$:
$$OC = AC - AO = 12 - 8 = 4\text{ cm}$$

Sum the three boundary lengths (Arc $BC$, straight edge $OC$, and radius $OB = 8\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } BC + OC + OB = 8.6728 + 4 + 8 = 20.6728 \approx 20.7\text{ cm} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$
